brief: Left by JS-158 (brief-triage-js158.md): three product statements its record read from code and saw in no run (the dead-node reap against the job end of a worker forgotten while it lives; a pending migration altering two worker tables in a rolling upgrade; a stream replica's snapshot read aborted by that migration); three test-kit minors (five forced checks passing on today's kit, cmd/jellyscale's guard not seeing Postgres sessions and the stress driver's fake workers outside it, fresh() restarting a kept worker); spec writers twice in one day matching mixed-case patterns against the lowercased doc, each stopping a build on a dispute.
tradeoff: Given up: nothing a viewer or operator has. Left as they are, on no data that anyone meets them: a stall of up to a lease (about 30 s, unverified) for the viewers of a job whose end a deadlock with the reap aborts, and up to 5 s in which a stream replica whose snapshot read a migration aborted cannot answer from memory if Postgres also goes away.
entry: No new task and no priority moved. JS-079 gains criterion 6: a migration that locks two tables a running worker and a stream replica use, applied under a playing film with real processes, leaves the upgrading replica started or refusing once with a message naming the lock, and no viewer request answered an error; what a replica answers from memory after an aborted snapshot read is recorded and returns as a brief, not built. JS-079 is split into migrations (1, 3, 6) and mixed-version play (2, 4, 5) when it starts. The reap against a live worker's job end is BL-260, promoted on a 40P01 on a job end in the dogfood's logs, a fault schedule or JS-175's counted runs, or on JS-165's observation, and then a criterion of JS-165. The snapshot gap is dropped as its own work. The three kit minors are dropped: the two checks that fail before the fix carry the proof, and a deadlock from the unguarded paths returns through JS-175 criterion 7. BL-178 closes, covered by JS-158. One line is added to .claude/agents/spec-writer.md after the running workflow ends: docs checks match a lowercased doc, so words and patterns are written in lower case; no build.js change. After JS-161, JS-166 is the next build, then JS-041; JS-174 takes only a gap when no build or reproduction holds the machine, else it is taken on the dogfood under JS-166 (its criterion 1); JS-160 stays behind unless JS-175's count shows more than 2 failures (D-058). Reopens on: a 40P01 on a job end or on a snapshot refresh logged on any deployment; a replica failing to start at a migration on the dogfood; a third spec dispute of the same kind.
serves: PRODUCT.md: 'Nothing breaks the viewers' evening. Upgrades, a lost machine and a database failover happen without interrupting anyone.' Owner, 2026-11-20: without data, keep the product as PRODUCT.md describes it and name the data that would change it. Owner, 2026-11-22: nothing outruns the product.
